prompt:
Design a magnetic closure mechanism for a leather tablet case. The case protects a 10.9-inch tablet (dimensions 248mm × 179mm × 6.1mm, weight 480g). The closure uses four neodymium disc magnets (N35 grade, 10mm diameter × 2mm thick) embedded in the leather flap, attracting to a steel shim plate (0.5mm mild steel) bonded inside the case body. The magnets are arranged in a 2×2 pattern at 20mm spacing.

Each N35 neodymium magnet (10mm × 2mm disc) has a rated pull force of approximately 1.5 kg (14.7 N) against a mild steel plate. Total closure force = 4 × 14.7 = 58.8 N, which provides secure closure against the flap weight (~30g) with large margin. The magnets are bonded into pockets in the leather using cyanoacrylate adhesive. The case includes a fold-back stand function where the flap folds behind the tablet for hands-free viewing. Please review the closure design.

seeded_faults.description: Four 10mm × 2mm N35 neodymium magnets at 20mm spacing create a combined magnetic field that extends several centimetres beyond the case surface. This field will interfere with the tablet's internal magnetometer (compass), which uses the Earth's magnetic field (~50µT) for orientation and location services. Neodymium magnets of this size produce fields of 50-200 mT at their surface and 1-5 mT at 20mm distance — orders of magnitude above the Earth's field. The tablet's compass will be permanently offset or non-functional while in the case. More critically, many modern tablets use hall-effect magnetic sensors to detect case closure (triggering sleep/wake). The four-magnet pattern may trigger unintended sleep/wake events depending on tablet orientation, or may interfere with the intended sleep/wake function if the magnet positions don't align with the tablet's sensor location. The magnet placement must be designed in conjunction with the specific tablet's sensor layout, not arbitrarily positioned.
seeded_faults.location_hint: Four N35 neodymium magnets at 20mm spacing adjacent to tablet.

seeded_faults.description: The rated pull force of 1.5 kg per magnet assumes ideal conditions: clean, flat contact between the magnet face and a thick steel plate, pulled directly normal to the surface. In this application, multiple factors reduce the actual force: (1) The 0.5mm steel shim is thinner than the optimal plate thickness for full flux capture — a 10mm × 2mm N35 magnet requires approximately 2-3mm of mild steel to fully close the magnetic circuit. At 0.5mm, the shim saturates magnetically and captures only 60-75% of the available flux, reducing pull force to approximately 1.0-1.1 kg per magnet. (2) The leather between the magnets and the shim adds an air gap of 1-2mm (leather thickness), further reducing pull force — neodymium magnet pull force drops approximately 50% per 1mm of air gap for small magnets. (3) The closure is opened by peeling (moment about the hinge edge), not by direct normal pull. Peel forces are typically 20-30% of normal pull force. The effective opening resistance is likely 3-5 N total, not 58.8 N — barely enough to keep the flap closed if the case is held upside down.
seeded_faults.location_hint: Pull force of 1.5 kg per magnet assumed under ideal conditions.

ground_truth_notes: Two faults: (1) Neodymium magnets will interfere with tablet magnetometer and may trigger unintended hall-effect sleep/wake events. Magnet placement must be designed to specific tablet sensor layout. Reference: Apple/Samsung tablet technical specifications (hall sensor locations); K&J Magnetics field calculator. (2) Rated pull force assumes ideal contact with thick steel plate. Thin shim (magnetic saturation), leather air gap, and peel-mode opening reduce effective force to ~5-10% of rated value. Reference: K&J Magnetics application notes on air gap and plate thickness; Supermagnete pull force testing methodology.
